result.process_summary: Both systems rely on a signal (bell ring / event) that activates a designated responder (waiter / event handler). The responder remains idle while other tasks proceed, and upon receiving its specific signal it interrupts its current activity to perform a predefined response. Multiple distinct signals map to distinct responders, yielding efficient, on‑demand processing.
potential_breaks: Human waiters may experience delays or forget to respond, whereas event handlers execute deterministically.
A bell typically alerts a single waiter, while multiple handlers can be attached to the same event.
The analogy does not capture concurrent handling of multiple events that can occur simultaneously in programming.
